correctness.rationale: In a connected bipartite graph an edge's endpoints have distances from a third vertex differing by exactly one, so a general-position set of size at least three is independent. In an independent selection here distinct points are distance two, selected point-line pairs distance three, and selected line-line pairs distance two if intersecting and four if parallel. The only possible additive equality is 4=2+2 for parallel end lines; a selected point cannot be distance two from them, while a selected line is distance two from both precisely if it is a common transversal. This proves the selected-line dichotomy. For b≥1 parallel lines the total mixed size is at most q²−b(q−1); with b different directions the union has size ≥bq−binom(b,2). For q≥4 the penalty b(q−1)−binom(b,2), concave on [2,q+1], exceeds q−1 at both endpoints, so only b=1 can attain q²−q+1. For q=3 the only possible extra equality is b=4 with distinct pairwise intersections. Adding the line at infinity would give five projective lines with no triple concurrency. Such a family covers 10 of the 13 points; on every family line each point is already a pairwise intersection. A pencil based at an uncovered point would therefore pair off the five lines, impossible. Thus maximizers are one line with all its off-line points, with q(q+1) choices. The all-line bound q+1 is smaller than q²−q+1 for q≥3, and every point subset is general position; this gives the unique full-point maximum and both coefficient formulas. At q=2, b≤2 gives mixed size at most three. Among eight different-direction triples, four are concurrent (one per point) and the remaining four cover three points each, giving four mixed maxima plus the pure point maximum. Exact independent metric enumeration returned (overall size, overall count, mixed size, mixed count)=(4,5,4,4) at q=2 and (9,1,7,12) at q=3, with coefficient 48 at degree seven for q=3.
residual_risks: Independent enumeration used Floyd–Warshall and exhaustively enumerated feasible subsets by geodesic-triple pruning, only for the two finite-field instances. The axiom-based proof, not enumeration or the supplied scripts, establishes generality.

evidence: Anand et al. characterize general position by complete induced components with an in-transitive, distance-constant partition. Their bipartite equality gp(G)=α(G) for diameter two or three does not include the affine incidence graph, which has diameter four. Iršič et al. develop the polynomial; their inspected Theorem 4.2 is for Kneser graphs K(n,2).
broader_coverage.reasoning: Anand's universal criterion does cover the affine structural test by a short metric reduction, but it is not an extremal or enumerative evaluation. The diameter equality and Kneser computation do not yield the exact first mixed coefficient or rigidity of its maximizers.

evidence: A bipartite edge component cannot have distance constant to a third vertex by parity. For the remaining singleton components the prior in-transitivity condition fails exactly at 4=2+2, for a parallel pair and a transversal. The once-subdivided theorem accounts for order two. The well-covered-dimension theorem is about weights on maximal independent sets, not general-position subsets.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The structural equivalence and order-two example are not credited as new; the surviving exact assertions already in the original finding are for q≥3. The general criterion alone does not optimize the union size of direction-restricted families or handle the odd-order projective obstruction at q=3, which are needed for the coefficient and uniqueness results.

originality.rationale: The general distance-partition criterion already covers the structural test by direct specialization, and the earlier once-subdivided complete-graph record explicitly covers the order-two maximum and polynomial. The distinct contribution is the affine-plane extremal argument and exact first mixed coefficient for arbitrary finite affine planes of order q≥3, not a new general-position criterion or the q=2 data.
residual_risks: A differently named or unindexed all-order computation is not ruled out; priority is not certified. The exact earlier order-two overlap and broader structural coverage are explicit exclusions from the originality judgment.

value.rationale: The point–line incidence graph is canonical for any finite affine plane, and the first degree admitting mixed selections measures a natural gap below the rigid maximum. The extremal classification identifies all configurations that close that gap, yielding the exact first mixed coefficient uniformly without field-coordinate assumptions. This is more than a computation at the already covered order-two graph or an application of the generic structural test alone.
residual_risks: No full polynomial for q≥3 or determination of the lower mixed coefficients is claimed.
